chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The woman who gives Khula (compensatory divorce) is the one who says to her husband, 'Divorce me, and I will give you whatever I have taken from you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him to take anything from her until she says,
By Allah, I will not fulfill a vow for you, and I will not obey you in a matter, and I will permit in your house without your permission, and I will settle in your bed another than you.

So when she does that without him knowing it, it is permissible for him whatever he takes from her, and it would be a divorce without a divorce following it. So she would be irrevocably divorced by that, and he would be a proposer from the proposers.

key_terms.اخْلَعْنِي: Divorce me (imperative form used in Khula context)
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةُ: The woman who gives Khula (compensatory divorce)
key_terms.خَاطِباً مِنَ الْخُطَّابِ: A proposer from the proposers (eligible to propose marriage again)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a husband to keep the dowry in a Khula divorce according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between a consensual Khula and a unilateral 'Khula of the wife' (Al-Mukhtaliqa), where the wife initiates separation. It establishes that the husband is entitled to retain the bride price only if the wife explicitly declares her intent to disrupt marital harmony—specifically by occupying the bed with another or entering without permission—thereby transforming the transaction into an irrevocable divorce (Talaq al-Ba'in) without requiring a formal verbal pronouncement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said, ‘

The woman divorced by Khul’a is the one who is saying to her husband, ‘Detach from me, and I will give you whatever I have taken from you’. Heasws said: ‘It is not Permissible for him that he takes anything from her until she is saying, ‘
By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I will not fulfill a vow for you, and will not obey you in a matter, and will permit in your house without your permission, and will settle in your bed other than you’.

So when she does that from without him knowing it (forcing her), it is permissible for him whatever he takes from her, and it would be a divorce without a divorce following it. So she would be irrevocably divorced by that, and he would be a proposer from the proposers’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The woman who is divorced by means of al-Khul‘, who says to her husband, ‘Divorce me and I pay what I have received from you.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not lawful for him to receive such payment until she says, ‘
By Allah, I will not honor your turn, will not obey any of your orders, will allow people to enter your house without your permission and will allow others to sleep in your bed.’

When she does this without informing him, then receiving payment from her is lawful, she is divorced once without any other divorce to follow, and she becomes a stranger. He is then one of those who can propose marriage with her.’”
